term: can be otherwise (ἐνδέχεται ἄλλως ἔχειν; aliter et aliter se habere)
definition: `CanBeOtherwise x r`: x can be otherwise in respect r. Metaphysics XII.7, 1072b4-8 says that what is moved can be otherwise, the first heaven in place though not in substance, and that the unmoved mover cannot be otherwise in any way; Aquinas counts the respects as substance, quantity, quality and place (In Metaph. XII, lect. 7 n. 12). A Lean primitive: it is not defined from act, potency or CanFailToBe, and no modal semantics is encoded. It is related to CanFailToBe only by the bridge STMT-WHAT-CAN-FAIL-TO-BE-CAN-BE-OTHERWISE, read from In Metaph. V, lect. 6 n. 14 (what can be in more ways can be otherwise and otherwise), and its weaker sibling STMT-WHAT-CAN-FAIL-TO-BE-CAN-BE-OTHERWISE-IN-SOME-RESPECT. Aquinas also gives the necessary as what cannot be otherwise (V, lect. 6 n. 6 and n. 14; Met. V.5, 1015a33-35).
